text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- German electronic company Siemens is expanding in Norway. Siemens A/S in Norway completed a financial year in September with a turnover on 3.4 billion crowns. Hans Loedrup, head of Siemens in Norway, expects the total turnover to be 4.0 billion crowns in two years and the number of employees to increase from 2,700 to over 3,000.

- Norway on Tuesday strongly condemned the killing of six foreign aid workers, including two Norwegian women, in Russia's breakaway republic Chechnya. Foreign Minister Bjoern Tore Godal said the murders posed a serious setback for humanitarian assistance and called for the perpetrators to be found and brought to trial.

- Berit Fosheim, deputy secretary in the Justice Department, resigned on Tuesday in a scandal over the national intelligence service's surveillance of a prominent left-wing politician, Berge Furre. Fosheim did not inform the then Justice Minister, Grete Faremo, about the surveillance of Berge Furre. Faremo resigned as Energy Minister on Monday to take constitutional responsibility for the scandal.

- Industrial group Norsk Hydro ASA said on Tuesday it had awarded a contract for work on the semi-submersible steel Troll C oil platform to Norway's Umoe Haugesund AS. The floating production unit (FPU) contract value is around 3.9 billion crowns, Norsk Hydro said.
- Knut Kloster jr. is planning to build a cruise ship called "The World" worth three billion crowns. The target group is companies and individuals who want their own apartment on board.
